summary: Generate typed TanStack Query hooks for a React app from an API's OpenAPI document, sent through the app's own fetch client.
description: Add Orval to a React single-page app so its API calls come from the backend's OpenAPI document as typed TanStack Query hooks. Generated calls go through the app's existing API client, so they keep its base URL, request ids, logging and error type. A drift check regenerates into a temporary directory and fails when the committed client is stale, and a second check fails until a page uses a generated hook. The API's document has to be copied into the app; generated calls rely on the document's types rather than runtime validation.
seoDescription: Generate typed TanStack Query hooks from an OpenAPI document with Orval for a React app, with a drift check that catches a stale client.

projectExamples.title: Team notes dashboard
projectExamples.description: A browser dashboard where a team lists, opens and writes notes, its screens reading from typed hooks generated from the notes API's published OpenAPI document.

plain.whatItIs: Writes the code a React website uses to call its server, from the server's own description of its requests, and checks that code stays up to date.
goodAt: Keeping a website's calls in step with what the server accepts
Catching a forgotten update before it ships
notGoodAt: Writing the server or its description; the API project does that.
Checking responses at runtime; it trusts the description's types.
